questions: Must RecordRunProgressChange executions retain the submitted list order, or must they be reordered by (node_id, map_index)?

quotes: The records one change writes take their store positions with every StoredValue first, in the order the variant names them, then the other records in the order the field-assignment note of its variant lists them, the elements of a list of records in list order (a RecordRunProgressChange's executions in (node_id, map_index) order); an update keeps the record's position, so positions never depend on record type or database insertion order.
RecordRunProgressChange writes its executions in (node_id, map_index) order with an absent map_index before index 0.
judgement.why: RecordRunProgressChange executions must be reordered by (node_id, map_index), with an absent map_index before index 0.

topics.topic: RecordSet inclusion or return of an existing unchanged StoredValue
questions: Must an existing unchanged StoredValue be returned, or must the RecordSet contain only records actually written or changed?

judgement.why: This asks the same question as P1 on unchanged text: an existing StoredValue is returned without being written again.

precedent.topic: Behavior and return value when record_change encounters an existing StoredValue identity
quotes: A StoredValue whose value_id already exists is not written again and the existing record is returned in its place, since equal values share one identity; spooled files must already be published in the run's spool by spool_file before the change that writes their SpooledFile records.

Any other broken invariant (a linked record missing, an identity already present for an immutable record, a status change from a status the change does not start from) or a failed transaction raises StoreInternalError with nothing written.
precedent.why: The specific StoredValue rule requires returning the existing record without rewriting it, while the phrase “Any other broken invariant” excludes that stated special case.

topics.topic: Whether a valid close-delimited 2xx response may succeed at end of stream instead of being treated as a transport failure
questions: Must every end of stream be treated as a transport failure, or must an end of stream that validly terminates a close-delimited 2xx response allow that response to succeed?

quotes: send_prepared_request: [BEHAVIOR] The outcome is decided in this order, with effect_class read meaning the read column: a failure of name resolution, connection or TLS before the first request byte was written is service_unreachable, attempt not_sent for other classes; a timeout, reset, end of stream, malformed status line or headers — a status line and header section longer together than the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SERVICE_RESPONSE_BYTES_MAX constant included —, or only 1xx after the first byte was written is service_unreachable for read and outcome_unknown with attempt unknown otherwise; 3xx is operation_failed with detail redirect_not_followed for read and outcome_unknown with attempt unknown otherwise; 5xx is service_unreachable for read and outcome_unknown with attempt unknown otherwise; 4xx is operation_refused, attempt not_applied for other classes; 2xx whose body is longer than the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SERVICE_RESPONSE_BYTES_MAX constant, whatever its output ports, or whose body as read contains the bytes of the credential value sent, searched before parsing, or whose outputs do not fit is contract_violation, attempt applied for other classes; 2xx whose outputs fit is succeeded, attempt applied for other classes.

send_prepared_request: [BEHAVIOR] A binding without output ports reads the body only up to one byte past the response ceiling, does not parse or validate it, and succeeds on 2xx unless the body is over the ceiling or contains the credential bytes sent, which is contract_violation.
judgement.why: A valid close-delimited 2xx response necessarily ends by end of stream, but one passage classifies end of stream as a transport failure while the other requires an otherwise acceptable 2xx response to succeed.

topics.topic: Whether multi-file FileListPayload spooling uses tuple indices as list_index or is forbidden
questions: How must a FileListPayload containing multiple files be spooled when every file is required to use the same SpooledFileKey with no list_index; should the behavior require each file's tuple index as list_index, or should file-list outputs be forbidden?

judgement.why: This asks the same unchanged question as P6 about whether FileListPayload outputs are forbidden or spooled with distinct list indexes.

precedent.topic: Whether file-list send outputs are supported and, if so, require distinct spool list indexes
quotes: SendResult fields (exact, no others exist): outcome: ServiceOutcome, attempt_status: AttemptStatus | None, detail_code: DetailCode | None, outputs: tuple[PortPayload, ...], failure_detail: str | None
FileListPayload fields (exact, no others exist): payload_kind: Literal['file_list'], port: str, contents: tuple[bytes, ...]

When the SendResult outcome is succeeded MUST store the outputs before writing: each JSON output whose canonical bytes exceed the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant turns the outcome into contract_violation with detail value_too_large and no outputs; otherwise each JSON output is published with put_value_bytes and becomes a StoredValue of value carriage with the output port's stored schema (M21: its value_schema, or for a many port the canonical array schema with it as items), its size and the class the binding declares for that port, and a file output is published with spool_file under SpooledFileKey of the run, node, map_index, this attempt_number, the port and no list_index, becoming a SpooledFile of the port's declared class, which every port of a binding has, since a proposal leaving out a port's class is refused (A08 rule 5, M01), so that class is always a DisclosureClass member; a RefusedError from spool_file turns the outcome into contract_violation with no outputs, a non-read binding's attempt still applied (a read binding has no attempt).

The NodeExecutionDraft has status the outcome name (= models.NodeExecutionStatus) — the SendResult's, or contract_violation when storing the outputs turned it so —, detail_code from the SendResult, or, when storing turned the outcome, value_too_large for an output over the stored value ceiling and None for a spool refusal; failure_detail from the SendResult, which is None for a succeeded one; executed the ExecutedBinding of the binding, inputs the given inputs, outputs, only when that outcome is succeeded, one StoredValuesRef or SpooledFilesRef per output port in port name order, a SpooledFilesRef with the class the binding declares for that port, and no outputs otherwise; and no resources_used.
precedent.why: The texts admit FileListPayload through SendResult's PortPayload outputs but specify neither rejection nor a collision-free storage rule for its multiple contents.

topics.topic: Whether optional X | None fields accept JSON null or advertise only X in tools/list inputSchema
questions: Must X | None fields accept JSON null, or must their advertised inputSchema exclude null by using only the schema of X?

quotes: for tools/call, the message names a catalogue operation and fits that operation's request model with no unknown field — a field typed X | None fitting when it is absent or JSON null — and every bound below, else invalid_request;
X | None the schema of X
judgement.why: The request-validation rule accepts JSON null for an optional field, while the advertised schema uses only X's schema and therefore excludes null.
